name: Jade
comment: The syntax of Jade 2.0.2, from compiler/src/frontend/lexer.rs and parser.rs. docs/jade-syntax-spec.md lists each construct and the scope it gets here.

expression.comment: Everything except line comments. Split out from the top-level list so f-string interpolations can reuse it: a `//` inside `{...}` as a comment rule would swallow the closing brace and quote and wreck the rest of the line. Order matters: the rules for a name in a particular place come before the general rules for keywords, types and calls.

escape-double.comment: The lexer accepts these escapes and no others; in a string it can escape only its own quote.
escape-double.name: constant.character.escape.jade

fescape-double.comment: An f-string also escapes its braces: \{ and \}.
fescape-double.name: constant.character.escape.jade

escape-invalid.comment: Any other escape is a compile error, so it is marked as one.
escape-invalid.name: invalid.illegal.escape.jade

fstring-interpolation.comment: The {expr} part of every f-string. `meta.embedded.line.jade` sits on top of the string scope so the theme rule for it resets the code inside to normal coloring; without it `f"x = {foo(bar)}"` renders as one run of string color.
fstring-interpolation.name: meta.embedded.line.jade

fstring-nested-braces.comment: Balances inner braces, such as a dict or class literal inside an interpolation, f"{Point { x: 1 }}", so the first inner `}` does not close the interpolation. The lexer counts braces the same way.

fstring-triple-double.comment: Triple-quoted forms come before single-quoted ones, so the closing quotes are not read as an empty string. `\b` keeps `buf"x"` a name and a string, as the lexer reads it.
fstring-triple-double.name: string.quoted.triple.jade

string-triple-double.comment: Every string may span lines; the triple-quoted forms only spare escaping the quote.
string-triple-double.name: string.quoted.triple.jade

prompt-member-deref.comment: obj~>p, the short form of obj.(?p): a prompt dereference on a member. Listed before the operators so `~` and `>` are not split into bitwise and comparison tokens.

prompt-deref.comment: ?p, and the `?` of obj.(?p). `?prompt "..."` is left to the keyword rule. A `?` before anything else, such as ?(a + b) or ?items[0], is colored by the operators rule.

exception-catch-typed.comment: catch TypeName binding: two names before the block. `catch e` has one, and falls to the keyword rule.

decorator.comment: @public on a class member, a type such as @int or @Animal, or any other decorator such as @tools::register or @retry(3). A decorator may share its line with what it decorates, `@public @int count`, so the rule stops at the end of the name; an argument list is left to the other rules.

patterns.comment: A capitalized name is a class, which declares the type of what it decorates.
patterns.name: entity.name.type.jade

class-declaration.comment: class Name, with an optional parent list that may span lines: class Dog(Animal, shapes.Pet).

patterns.comment: The last name of each parent; `shapes` in `shapes.Pet` is the file it comes from.
patterns.name: entity.other.inherited-class.jade

function-declaration.comment: fn name(params), or fn Type::method(params) for a method defined outside its class, where Type may be qualified: fn shapes.Point::area(). The parameter list may span lines, and each parameter may have a default.

patterns.comment: A parameter is the first name in the list, after a comma, or at the start of a line.

parameter-nested.comment: Brackets inside a default value, such as `b = f(1, c)` or `d = [1, e]`, so their commas do not start a parameter and their `)` does not end the list.

is-test.comment: x is Dog, a class test, where the class may be qualified: x is shapes.Dog.

removed-quoted-import.comment: use "file.jde" and from "file.jde" use ... were removed; imports name a module with :: notation, such as use std::math.

removed-keywords.comment: struct, extend and interface were removed in favor of class, and the `as` import alias was removed. The lexer still reads them so the compiler can name the replacement; they are marked removed rather than colored as working keywords.
removed-keywords.name: invalid.deprecated.removed.jade

patterns.comment: The same jade green as ? and ~>.
patterns.name: keyword.other.prompt.jade

patterns.comment: The lexer reads these as &&, || and !, and `is` tests a class.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.word.jade

storage-types.comment: The built-in types: conversions such as int(x), pipe targets such as ?p |> int, and decorators such as @int. Not after a dot, where the name is a field.
storage-types.name: storage.type.jade

constants-nil.comment: nil, None and null are three spellings of the same value.
constants-nil.name: constant.language.null.jade

numbers.comment: Decimal integers and floats with digits on both sides of the point. Jade has no hex, binary, exponent or underscore forms.

support-functions.comment: The globals a program has without an import, from compiler/src/core/mod.rs, plus join. Not after a dot, so list.join(",") stays a method call.
support-functions.name: support.function.builtin.jade

support-classes.comment: Grammar, the one built-in class: Grammar.new(pattern).
support-classes.name: support.class.builtin.jade

type-reference.comment: A capitalized name before {, ( or :: is a class: a literal Point { x: 1 }, a view Animal(d), or a member Account::new and Parent::m().

function-call.comment: name(...): plain calls, method calls such as bird.speak(), and the last part of a path such as Account::new(...). `\b` matches after `.` and `:` as it does after a space, so only the callee is captured. It comes after the keyword, type and built-in rules, which match the same shape.

patterns.comment: The base of a copy-with literal: Config { ...c, port: 9090 }.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.spread.jade

patterns.comment: Paths and class members: std::time, Account::new, @tools::register.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.path.jade

patterns.comment: ~> and a ? that prompt-deref did not take. Before the bitwise and comparison rules so ~> stays one token.
patterns.name: keyword.other.prompt.jade
